1. What is the sum of the number of students who scored 70 or more than
70 but less than 80 marks
in Hindi and the number of students who scored 80 or more than 80
marks in Punjabi?
(1) 330
(2) 228
(3) 272
(4) 284
Answer Key: (2)
Solution:
Students scoring 70–80 in Hindi
Hindi students scoring:
• 70 and above = 264
• 80 and above = 108
So,
264 – 108 = 156
Students scoring 80 and above in Punjabi
15% of total students scored 80 and above.
15% of 1200:
15/100 × 1200 = 180
Out of these, Hindi students = 108
So, Punjabi students:
180 – 108 = 72
Required sum
156 + 72 = 228
Hence, the correct answer is 228.
Hence, option (2) is correct.

2. What is the ratio of the number of students who scored 50 or more than
50 marks but less than 60
marks in Hindi to the number of students who scored 40 or more than 40
marks but less than 50
marks in Punjabi?
(1) 12:11
(2) 8:7
(3) 3:1
(4) 13 :5
Answer Key: (4)
Solution:
Hindi students scoring 50–60
Hindi students:
• 50 and above = 554
• 60 and above = 424
So,
554 – 424 = 130
Punjabi students scoring 40–50
Total students scoring:
• 40 and above = 1200
• 50 and above = 90% of 1200
90/100 × 1200 = 1080
So, students scoring 40–50 overall:
1200 – 1080 = 120
Hindi students scoring 40–50:
624 – 554 = 70
So, Punjabi students scoring 40–50:
120 – 70 = 50
Required ratio
130:50
Divide by 10:
13:5
Hence, the correct answer is 13: 5.
Hence, option (4) is correct.

3. The number of students who scored 80 and above marks in Hindi
is________% less than the number of students who scored 60 or more
than 60 marks but less than 70 marks in Punjabi.
(1) 46
(2) 54
(3) 44
(4) 52
Answer Key: (1)
Solution:
Hindi students scoring 80 and above
Given directly: 108
Punjabi students scoring 60–70
Total students scoring:
• 60 and above = 65% of 1200
65/100 × 1200 = 780
• 70 and above = 35% of 1200
35/100 × 1200 = 420
So total students scoring 60–70:
780 – 420 = 360
Hindi students scoring 60–70:
424 – 264 = 160
So Punjabi students scoring 60–70:
360 – 160 = 200
Percentage less
Formula:
Difference / Larger value ×100
200 – 108 = 92
92/200 ×100 = 46%
Hence, the number of Hindi students scoring 80 and above is
46% less.
Hence, option (1) is correct.

4. What is the difference between the number of students who scored 70 or
more than 70 marks but less than 80 marks in Punjabi and the number
of students who scored 40 or more than 40 marks but less than 50
marks in Hindi?
(1) 20
(2) 16
(3) 14
(4) 30
Answer Key: (3)
Solution:
Punjabi students scoring 70–80
Total students scoring:
• 70 and above = 35% of 1200, 35/100 × 1200 = 420
• 80 and above = 15% of 1200, 15/100 × 1200 = 180
So total students scoring 70–80:
420 – 180 = 240
Hindi students scoring 70–80:
264 – 108 = 156
So Punjabi students scoring 70–80:
240 – 156 = 84
Hindi students scoring 40–50
624 – 554 = 70
Difference
84 – 70 = 14
Hence, the correct answer is 14.
Hence, option (3) is correct.

5. What is the average of the number of students who scored 50 or more
than 50 marks but less than 60 marks in Punjabi and the number of
students who scored 50 or more than 50 marks but less than 60 marks in
Hindi?
(1) 180
(2) 150
(3) 200
(4) 140
Answer Key: (2)
Solution:
Hindi students scoring 50–60
554 – 424 = 130
Punjabi students scoring 50–60
Total students scoring:
• 50 and above = 1080
• 60 and above = 780
So total students scoring 50–60:
1080 – 780 = 300
Punjabi students scoring 50–60:
300 – 130 = 170
Average
130 + 170 = 300
300/2 = 150
Hence, the correct answer is 150.
Hence, option (2) is correct.
